title: The Four-Piece Cold Email Checklist: Offer, List, Setup, Copy
description: The four-piece checklist from the reel: offer, list, setup and copy. Check each piece before you send so booked calls follow.
lead: This is the full four-piece checklist from the reel. A cold email system books calls only when the offer, the list, the setup and the copy all fit. Here's how to check each piece in the right order, with a test for every one.
insider: We check these four pieces before every client campaign, in this order. For one construction software client that meant **31 sales-qualified demos and 6 signed annual contracts** from 162,073 emails. The checklist is the easy part. Building the list, running the inboxes and answering every reply is the work we do for clients.

blocks.text: Why most campaigns only fix one piece

Most people spend all their time on the email copy. It's the part you can see. But copy is the last piece, not the first. A perfect email sent to the wrong people, from an inbox that lands in spam, about an offer nobody understands, books nothing.

Cold email still works when all four pieces fit. [Instantly's 2026 benchmark report](https://instantly.ai/cold-email-benchmark-report-2026) puts the average reply rate at **3.43%**, with the top quarter at **5.5% or more**. Instantly notes that the top group shows **better targeting**. That's a list piece, not a copy piece.

blocks.text: **Why it comes first:** the offer decides who you target and what you write. If a buyer can't repeat your offer in one sentence, no copy will save it.

blocks.label: One-sentence offer template
blocks.text:
We help [type of company] get [one result they want] in [time frame], without [the thing they hate doing].

Example: We help IT service firms book 10 sales calls a month, without hiring an SDR.

items: Fill in the template above.
Read it to someone outside your business and ask them to repeat it back.
If they can't, cut words until they can.
**Pass test:** a stranger repeats it correctly after one read.

blocks.text: **Why:** small, focused lists win. [Hunter's 2026 report](https://hunter.io/the-state-of-cold-email), based on 31 million emails, found sequences with **21 to 50 recipients got a 6.2% reply rate vs 2.4%** for sequences with 500+ recipients. The smaller list let senders write for one type of buyer.

items: Write down one buyer: industry, company size and job title.
Build a list of only those people. Split anything different into its own campaign.
Verify every email address before sending. Hunter's average bounce rate was **3.6%**. Instantly says keep bounces **under 2%**.
**Pass test:** you can describe everyone on the list in one sentence, and the list is verified.

blocks.text: **Why:** the setup decides inbox or spam. [Google's sender guidelines](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126) require SPF or DKIM for all senders, and SPF, DKIM and DMARC for anyone sending 5,000+ messages a day to Gmail. Google also says to start with low volume and increase slowly.

items: Send from separate domains, never your main business domain.
Set SPF, DKIM and DMARC on every sending domain. Our [DNS records guide](/blog/dns-records-for-cold-email.html) has the values.
Warm up every new inbox for at least 2 weeks before the first cold email.
Ramp up slowly. Instantly suggests starting at 5 to 10 emails a day and building up over 4 to 6 weeks.
**Pass test:** all three records check out in a DNS checker and warm-up has run for 2+ weeks.

blocks.text: **Why it's last:** once the offer, list and setup are right, copy is easy. You're writing to one type of person about one clear result. Instantly found top campaigns keep first emails **under 80 words** with a single call to action.

blocks.label: First email template (under 80 words)
blocks.text:
Subject: [their company] + [result]

Hi [first name],

[One line that shows you know their world, e.g. "Most IT firms your size win clients through referrals."]

We help [type of company] get [result] in [time frame], without [pain].

[One short proof line, only if it's real.]

Worth a quick chat next week?

[Your name]

items: Count the words. Under 80, or cut.
One question at the end. No links, no attachments in email 1.
Plan 4 to 7 emails in the sequence. Instantly found **42% of replies come from follow-ups**.
**Pass test:** a reader can tell who it's for and what they get within 5 seconds.

blocks.label: Order matters
blocks.text: Fix the pieces in order: offer, list, setup, copy. Each piece depends on the one before it.
Worked example: what a full picture can look like
Say you send to **1,000 verified buyers** and hit Instantly's average reply rate of **3.43%**.

items: In our full-quarter case study, about 1 in 4 replies came from a buyer who wanted to talk (1,061 of 4,372).
34 × 24% = **about 8 interested buyers** from 1,000 emails.
Now break one piece. If the setup fails and half your emails land in spam, the same 1,000 emails reach only 500 inboxes, and replies fall to about 17.

faq.q: Which piece should I fix first?
faq.a: The offer. It decides who goes on the list and what the email says. Then the list, then the setup, then the copy.

faq.q: My copy is good but I get no replies. Why?
faq.a: Usually the setup. If emails land in spam, nobody sees them. Check SPF, DKIM, DMARC and warm-up first.

faq.q: How big should my list be?
faq.a: Start small and focused. Hunter found sequences with 21 to 50 recipients got 6.2% replies vs 2.4% for 500+. Split big lists into small groups of one buyer type.
